turns.doctor_question: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response: Hi, doctor. Um, I'm here because I've started planning my days around not using elevators. It's just getting to be a problem. Like, I've been taking five flights of stairs at my apartment building instead of just riding up. I even turned down a training workshop I was supposed to lead because it was in a high-rise. And... I recently stopped doing visits with one of my older computer students because his building doesn't really have another option besides the elevator. So, yeah, I just figured it was time to talk to someone about it.

symptom_reasoning.S064: The patient clearly describes actively avoiding elevators by taking five flights of stairs, declining a workshop in a high-rise, and stopping home visits to a student.

turns.doctor_question: When you think about getting into an elevator, what specifically worries you most — is it the enclosed space itself, or is it more about being trapped or stuck with other people around you?
turns.patient_response: Um, it's definitely more about getting trapped. Or even dropped. Like, logically, I know an elevator in a regular office block is probably completely safe. But when I look at those older doors—like the ones in my apartment building, or the ones at work—my mind just instantly treats it like I'm about to get trapped in there, or the whole thing is going to fall. Even though part of me knows that sounds pretty over the top, I just can't shake that feeling when I'm standing in front of them.

symptom_reasoning.S062: The patient describes an irrational fear of elevators (getting trapped or falling) that they recognize as disproportionate to the actual danger, confirming a specific phobic fear.

turns.doctor_question: Besides elevators, do you experience similar anxiety or avoidance in other enclosed spaces — like small rooms, closets, airplanes, or crowded public transit?
turns.patient_response: No, not really. It's just elevators. I don't have any problem with small rooms or closets or anything like that. I fly a couple times a year to visit my parents, and being on a plane doesn't bother me at all. And I take the subway to work every day, even when it's packed, and I feel totally fine. It's really just the elevators that get to me.

turns.doctor_question: How long have you been experiencing this fear of elevators? Can you remember when it started?
turns.patient_response: It's been going on for about seven months now. It started pretty shortly after I moved into my current apartment—the one on the fifth floor. I had this... well, an elevator scare right around that time, and ever since then, it's just been an issue.

turns.doctor_question: When you're about to get on an elevator or even just thinking about it, do you notice physical symptoms like your heart racing, sweating, difficulty breathing, or feeling dizzy?
turns.patient_response: Yeah, I do. As soon as I step toward an elevator, or even just hear the doors clunk open, my chest tightens up right away. My hands get pretty sweaty, too. It's like I feel this sudden rush of panic before I've even had time to really think it through.

symptom_reasoning.S063: The patient describes an immediate rush of panic and physiological symptoms (chest tightness, sweaty hands) triggered right away upon approaching an elevator or hearing its doors.

turns.doctor_question: Outside of elevators, have you ever had sudden episodes of panic or intense fear that seemed to come out of nowhere, or do these panic symptoms only happen when you're dealing with elevators?
turns.patient_response: No, it's really just the elevators. I've never had a panic attack or felt that way out of the blue. It only happens when I'm faced with having to get in an elevator. Otherwise, I feel completely fine.
